злато.text:

Doublet of зо́лото (zóloto) and зло́то (zlóto).

sources.quote: From Old East Slavic колико (koliko), from Proto-Slavic *koliko. Doublet of кі́лько (kílʹko).

скільки.text: From Old East Slavic колико (koliko), from Proto-Slavic *koliko. Doublet of кі́лько (kílʹko).

sources.quote: Inherited from Old Ruthenian жаръ (žar), from Old East Slavic жаръ (žarŭ), from Proto-Slavic *žārъ, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰēr- (“heat”, root noun), from *gʷʰer- (“heat, hot”), whence also Proto-Slavic *gorěti, whence Ukrainian горі́ти (horíty, “to burn”).
sources.note: Wiktionary (en), CC BY-SA 4.0, автори статті — на сторінці; витяг Wiktextract/kaikki.org 2026-10-03

жар.text: Inherited from Old Ruthenian жаръ (žar), from Old East Slavic жаръ (žarŭ), from Proto-Slavic *žārъ, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰēr- (“heat”, root noun), from *gʷʰer- (“heat, hot”), whence also Proto-Slavic *gorěti, whence Ukrainian горі́ти (horíty, “to burn”).
